facts.text: Lederach was formally founded in 1825 by Henry Lederach, who built a house, blacksmith shop, and general store at the key crossroads.
The village grew into a stagecoach hub on the Philadelphia‑Norristown‑Allentown route, earning the nickname Lederachville in the 19th century.
Andrew Lederach, a Swiss‑German immigrant, first settled the area in 1718, buying 100 acres and starting the Pennsylvania German farming community.
The Lederach Golf Club, a public course amid rolling hills, reflects the community’s blend of historic architecture and modern recreation.
Lederach sits at a five‑way intersection of PA Route 113, Salfordville, Morris, Old Skippack, and Cross Roads, a landmark for local navigation.
Lower Salford Township recently secured nearly $2 million for a shared‑use path connecting to Lederach, highlighting ongoing community development.
